# Newton's Law of Cooling

Newton's law of cooling states that the rate of heat loss of a body is directly
proportional to the difference in temperature between the body and its
surroundings. This yields an exponential decay of temperature toward the ambient
temperature. The characteristic constant k governs how fast the object cools.

## Model

The temperature over time follows T of t equals T_env plus the initial gap times
the exponential of minus k times t. This exponential form is why cooling is fast
at first and then slows as the object approaches ambient temperature.
